correctness.rationale: The published rank convention gives R_w(i,j)=#{k<=i:w(k)<=n+1-j}. A diagonal congruence action with base-3-separated weights preserves every north-east rank condition and has exactly the symmetric coordinate points as projective fixed points. For S_ab with a<b, the north-east submatrix rank can only be 0, 1, or 2; monotonicity of R_w reduces all rank-one constraints to R_w(a,b)>=1 and all rank-two constraints to R_w(b,a)>=2. Diagonal points always survive by a pigeonhole argument. Translating the two inequalities gives the minimum and second-minimum prefix conditions. The extremal classifications are proved directly, and the packaged checker independently evaluates every north-east rank condition for all permutations through n=7.

value.rationale: Symmetric matrix Schubert varieties are a natural type-C counterpart of ordinary matrix Schubert varieties and occur in algebraic statistics through Gaussian conditional-independence models. The theorem gives a closed global topological invariant for every permutation and exposes a genuinely new two-order-statistic mechanism caused by the rank-two behavior of off-diagonal symmetric coordinate points. The sharp range is qualitatively different from the ordinary matrix case: the minimum collapses to n and the ambient maximum occurs exactly when w(1)=1. This is a uniform structural classification for a classical permutation-indexed family, not a small-rank or arbitrary numerical slice.
